reviews.rationale: Upheld on the supplied provisional working texts. The complete EO 7431 text (0-1475) identifies George C. Havenner, liaison officer, Government Printing Office, closes with number 7431 and is signed August 17, 1936. Its sole operative command couples exemption from section 204 with continuance until October 1, 1937; the exact ending span 1276-1367 says that date. The recited statute supplies authority and the retirement-age recital supplies context, with no independent surviving presidential command or concrete separate earlier-ending condition. This is a direct whole-command calendar limitation, not a performance deadline: legal expiration does not require proof that service continued through the cap. Actual earlier separation remains unproved and is distinct from a textual legal ending. The complete EO 7704 text (0-1488), signed September 10, 1937, identifies the same person and prior order and independently grants a further exemption until October 1, 1938. It does not expressly revoke or rewrite EO 7431 or establish uninterrupted service. Its separate authority does not carry EO 7431 past its own term. No independent post-term duty or express savings provision appears; any actually earned rights are conditional accrued consequences, not continuing operative authority. Accordingly the supplied own-terms end date and terminated/no operative status at the October 14, 2026 cutoff are supported, subject to the stated search, authentication and date-boundary qualifications.

reviews.rationale: Rejected as the exact whole-case claim. EO 7420 is identified by its complete text (0-1492), William T. Marshall, his Public Works position, closing number 7420 and July 20, 1936 signing line. But both the operative sentence and recital limit exemption and continuance to August 1, 1937. In particular the verified cited span 1325-1386 reads: thereof and continue him in the service until August 1, 1937. It does not say July 20, 1936. Both operative_clauses[0].first_end.date and whole_order_end.date instead assert 1936-07-20, and their rationales/source note falsely attribute that signing date to the ending span. This is a substantive claim-to-source contradiction despite successful byte/span binding. The complete EO 7629 text (0-1512), signed June 8, 1937, recites the earlier one-year exemption and independently grants a further period until August 1, 1938; neither its signing nor its separate cap proves an earlier end of EO 7420. The original contains one coupled fixed-term grant, no independent post-term command, express savings provision, or concrete separate earlier-ending condition. Actual separation and accrued rights remain unproved. The terminated/no operative cutoff status is compatible with the read calendar limitation, but does not rescue the exact first-ending claim. The source-supported August 1, 1937 cap is identified solely to explain rejection; no claim was repaired.
